turns.text: Thresholds are rules, not recall, so I will let the tool compute this rather than estimate it.

Ten obligations apply on this corpus. Grouped by what drives them.

Because you are a registered business: file an annual income tax return by 30 June (DOC-TAX-01#S1).

Because turnover of 3,200,000 sits between the 1,000,000 floor and the VAT threshold: turnover tax, monthly, by the 20th of the following month (DOC-TAX-01#S3). Note what this means in the other direction. You are below the VAT threshold on these figures, so VAT registration is not triggered yet (DOC-TAX-01#S2). Worth watching, because it is a turnover test and it moves with you.

Because you have 4 employees: PAYE (DOC-PAY-01#S1), health contributions (DOC-PAY-01#S2), pension contributions (DOC-PAY-01#S3) and the housing levy (DOC-PAY-01#S4). Four separate filings, all due by the 9th of the following month (DOC-PAY-01#S5). Also written contracts and employment records (DOC-EMP-01#S1, DOC-EMP-01#S2).

Because you handle personal data: the controller duties, including answering a data subject request within 30 days (DOC-DPA-01#S3, DOC-DPA-01#S4). Registration itself is not triggered at 4 employees and this turnover (DOC-DPA-01#S1), but the duties do not depend on registration.

Because you trade from premises in the food sector: the single business permit, renewed annually by 31 March (DOC-PERMIT-01#S1, DOC-PERMIT-01#S2), plus the food hygiene licence and food handler certificates (DOC-PERMIT-01#S3, DOC-SECTOR-01#S1). The certificates run on a 6 month cycle, which is the one here that is easiest to let lapse.

This corpus is synthetic, written for a software demonstration, so this is a worked example and not legal advice.
